info.title: Biohub Local Scoring Support Pack
info.subtitle: Score your cell tracker on train with the exact competition metric, on CPU
info.description:
# Biohub Local Scoring Support Pack

The [biohub cell-tracking competition](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/biohub-cell-tracking-during-development) scores a node-and-edge lineage graph with a custom edge-and-division metric, and there is no way to know your number without spending a submission. This pack fixes that: a drop-in `local_score(submission, gt_dir)` that wraps the organisers' OWN scoring code, so you get the exact metric on the train split, in seconds, on CPU.

## What is inside

- **local_score.py** the fork-magnet. `local_score("my_train_submission.csv", TRAIN_DIR)` returns the exact `score = adjusted_edge_jaccard + 0.1 * division_jaccard`, plus per-dataset rows. Reads each dataset's voxel scale from its metadata and drops dangling edges, exactly like the official evaluator.
- **tracking_cellmot/** the organisers' scoring package, vendored verbatim (three files, self-contained) under its own BSD 3-Clause LICENSE. Because this is their code and not a reimplementation, the number cannot drift from the leaderboard. Credit and copyright are theirs (github.com/royerlab/kaggle-cell-tracking-competition).
- **dataset_stats.csv** derived, aggregate summaries of the 199 train ground-truth graphs: node, edge and division counts, timepoints, voxel scale, the estimated true node count, and nodes per frame. This is where you see how sparsely the ground truth is labelled, which is why a clean prediction can score above 1.0.
- **make_stats.py** regenerates that table over any ground-truth directory.
- **metric_cheatsheet.md** the whole metric on one page, in plain words.
- **submission_template.csv** the exact submission row format, one node example and one edge example.

## Quick use, on Kaggle with internet on

```python
import numpy as np, subprocess, sys
NPV = np.__version__   # pin numpy so the install cannot break the image ABI
subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", "-q", "tracksdata==0.1.0rc6", "polars", "geff", f"numpy=={NPV}"])
import sys; sys.path.append("/kaggle/input/biohub-local-scoring-support-pack")
from local_score import local_score
TRAIN = "/kaggle/input/competitions/biohub-cell-tracking-during-development/train"
summary, rows = local_score("my_train_submission.csv", TRAIN)
print(summary["score"])
```

## Provenance and rules

Nothing here is competition data. The scorer is public BSD-3 source, the cheatsheet and glue are my own writing, `dataset_stats.csv` is transformative aggregate statistics (counts and medians, never coordinates or images), and the template is synthetic. Companion notebook that explains and demonstrates the scorer: [Score your cell tracker locally](https://www.kaggle.com/code/busyaprime/score-your-cell-tracker-locally).
